svg.text: Dataflow Graph ML Framework - tf.function + XLA + TFRT - Google / OpenXLA
Python to PolymorphicFunction - trace on call
Eager + Graph Dual Mode (TF2 default eager)
Imperative UX with graph performance via @tf.function
mlir_to_bef - MLIR lowered to BEF binary format
Host Runtime drives CPU/GPU/TPU device runtimes
service API for distributed data loading
Decouples I/O from compute on accelerator
GPU Device Runtime - stream + memcpy + kernel launch
TPU Device Runtime - infeed/outfeed + XLA pod
Fully async - kernels run when args available
Graph-first design: dataflow DAG enables fusion, constant folding, and cross-platform deployment
TF2: eager by default - @tf.function switches to optimized graph execution
Step 1: @tf.function decorated Python fn called with Tensor inputs
Step 2: AutoGraph converts Python control flow (if/for) to graph ops
Step 3: Trace builds tf.Graph (FuncGraph) - record TF ops - skip pure Python
Step 4: Wrap as ConcreteFunction - cache per input signature/shape/dtype
Step 5: Execute via TFRT/XLA - subsequent calls reuse compiled graph (no retrace)
Retracing on new shapes is expensive - use input_signature to limit variants
Keras model.compile(jit_compile=True) enables XLA for entire training step
Train once as graph - deploy everywhere via SavedModel export pipeline
XLA fusion example: mul+add+reduce fused into single GPU kernel - fewer memory round-trips
tensorflow/tensorflow - Google - CUDA/TPU/CPU/Edge - TF Serving + TFLite + TFX - OpenXLA consortium
Eager path: op-by-op dispatch - GradientTape - device placement - immediate execution
Graph path: tf.function trace - Grappler - XLA fuse - TFRT BEF execute - SavedModel deploy
Sources: tensorflow.org guides - TFRT design doc - OpenXLA tf2xla - tf.function API - TF Serving
